Notes: Early 18th century: Jewish community of Woronow numbered 70 souls; year is midpoint of 'early 18th century'; source says Jewish town came into being mid-17th century (Year Established)
Late 19th century: 250 families (approx. 1200 people); year is an approximation of 'late 19th century'
333 Jews and 117 Catholics of 468 total inhabitants
333 Jews of 468 residents (as stated in source; same figure ruwiki dates to 1865); two synagogues in the 1880s
'1940s' 350 families and 1600 people; year approximated as 1940 (pre-war)

Voronovo ghetto existed summer 1941 to 11 May 1942; Vilnius deportees also brought in Nov 1941; 268 Jews murdered 14 Nov 1941 (sources vary 263-800); on 11 May 1942 about 2700 Jews assembled and 1291 (other source 1885) killed - flows and death tolls not used as Population; Soviet commission: 1604 Jews executed in Voronovo district
Mass grave of 1835 martyrs killed 11 May 1942 (death toll; may include non-residents)
By 1946 the town's Jewish community was entirely destroyed; survivors scattered to DP camps and Israel; 'approximately three thousand Jews' murdered there (toll, not used as population)
